matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal). Changing the orientation would create an invalid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Apply whenever you relocate a stick; check that its orientation stays the same.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick and rotating it to become horizontal, turning an I into a minus sign.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Apply to enforce the single‑stick‑move constraint before finalising the transformation.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a numeral without placing it elsewhere, causing a missing character.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Check each character after the move to ensure it remains a recognized numeral or operator.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with only one diagonal after moving a stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds after the transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a syntactically valid equation, compute its numeric value to confirm it is true.
matchstick.example: Accepting an equation like 'V = XVI - X' without checking that 5 ≠ 6.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain both diagonals so the character remains a valid X or V.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a move involves a diagonal stick from or to an X or V, ensure the character still has two diagonals.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal stick from an X, leaving a single diagonal line, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' (upper‑cased, whitespace‑collapsed).
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the very end of the answer, before submitting.
matchstick.example: Ending the response with 'Correct version: V = X' missing the required prefix and exact format.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (a single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave a half‑I shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider taking a stick from an I, delete the whole I and use the stick elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Moving the only stick from an I and leaving a half‑I shape.

matchstick.title: Transfer vertical stick between I's
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick from one I (which then disappears) to another I creates II (or adds to an existing I). The source I is removed, the target gains a second vertical stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase the count of I's on one side while reducing it on the other.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to another I but forgetting to delete the source I, resulting in an extra I.

matchstick.title: Diagonal stick reposition for V↔X
matchstick.principle: When a V or X appears, you can change it to the other by moving one of its diagonal sticks to a new position that makes the two diagonals cross (V→X) or meet at a point (X→V). Preserve the diagonal orientation and keep exactly two diagonal sticks in the character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Apply when the equation contains a V or X and converting it to the other could resolve the arithmetic mismatch.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal stick from a V, leaving it with a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from I to V/X to create VI or XI
matchstick.principle: If the equation can be balanced by adding an I after a V or X, move a vertical stick from an existing I (which disappears) to the right of the V or X, forming VI or XI. Ensure the source I is removed entirely and the target numeral remains a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Apply when you need to add an I after a V or X to make the equality hold and there is an extra I elsewhere that can supply a vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to a V but leaving the original I unchanged, resulting in an extra I.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving sticks without checking the resulting numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a transformation, compute the Arabic values of both sides and confirm they match.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets the required prefix or exact whitespace handling.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>'.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick but does not place it elsewhere, effectively removing it.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that every moved stick is placed to form a valid character or operator.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape (e.g., V with one diagonal, X with one diagonal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick from a numeral without preserving its required components.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick from a numeral, keep the remaining sticks such that the character remains a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid Roman numeral (e.g., IIII, invalid ordering)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assembles symbols that do not conform to Roman numeral rules.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving sticks, verify that each numeral follows standard Roman numeral syntax.
